channel.title: SEO guides by Christopher Abraham
channel.description: Guides to indexing, audits, schema, redirects, site speed, and AI search

item.title: How to read the Page indexing report in Search Console
item.description: A field guide to Search Console's Page indexing report: what each exclusion reason means, which ones need action, and how to find the template behind them.

item.title: The AI search readiness checklist
item.description: A practical checklist for AI search: crawler access, server rendered content, entity schema, answer shaped pages, llms.txt, outside evidence, and measurement.

item.title: What a technical SEO audit should give you
item.description: How to tell a useful technical SEO audit from a tool export: a clear question, evidence for each finding, a ranked plan, developer tickets, and a plain summary.

item.title: The schema markup a small business actually needs
item.description: Which schema types a small business needs, which to skip, and example structured data for local businesses, services, FAQs, and breadcrumbs, kept accurate.

item.title: Ten rules for 301 redirects that keep your rankings
item.description: Ten rules for 301 redirects in migrations and redesigns: map one to one, avoid chains, keep redirects for years, use 410 on purpose, and test in bulk.

item.title: Core Web Vitals in plain English
item.description: Core Web Vitals explained without jargon: what LCP, INP, and CLS measure, why lab scores differ from field data, the usual causes, and the fixes that work.

item.title: How to correct what AI search says about you
item.description: When ChatGPT, Gemini, or Google's AI Overviews get your facts wrong, here is how to find where the error came from and publish corrections that get picked up.

item.title: One person, two names: entity SEO for pen names and nicknames
item.description: How to make Google and AI assistants see that Christopher and Chris, or a pen name and a legal name, are one person, using schema, sameAs, and consistency.

item.title: Proving expertise with third-party sources
item.description: Your own claims carry little weight with Google and AI assistants. University news, vendor case studies, old bios, and bylines do. How to find and use them.

item.title: How to write an About page that search engines and AI trust
item.description: A recipe for an About page that Google and AI assistants quote correctly: current work first, verifiable facts, outside sources, schema, and no guesswork.

item.title: Launch a site on a parked domain with Cloudflare and GitHub Pages
item.description: Step by step: take a domain off a parking page, move DNS to Cloudflare, point it at GitHub Pages, get HTTPS, and avoid the caching traps on launch day.

item.title: How to lock down a domain that never sends email
item.description: Four DNS records stop spammers from forging mail from a domain you never send from: a null MX, an SPF that allows nothing, strict DMARC, and an empty DKIM key.

item.title: What happens to your old domains when they lapse
item.description: When an old company or project domain expires, drop catchers buy it for its links and reputation. What they do with it, the harm, and how to protect yourself.

item.title: How to write an llms.txt file
item.description: What llms.txt is, who reads it, and how to write one: the format, the full text companion file, Markdown page copies, robots.txt rules, and common mistakes.

item.title: Meta keywords in 2026: ignored, mostly harmless, used honestly
item.description: Google ignores the meta keywords tag and Bing has called stuffing it a spam signal. Why some sites still use it, and how to write one that does no harm at all.

item.title: Website accessibility without overlays
item.description: Build accessibility into a small business website instead of bolting on an overlay: contrast, headings, links, images, keyboard use, forms, and testing it.

item.title: Accessibility as SEO: the search, AI, and trust dividends
item.description: WCAG fixes pay off more than once: alt text, headings, link text, labels, and captions lift rankings, AI answers, agent browsing, and trust, and cut legal risk.

item.title: The Lynx test: see your website the way crawlers and AI read it
item.description: Lynx, a text browser, shows what search engines and AI crawlers that skip JavaScript receive. How to install it, what to check, and online alternatives.

item.title: How to hire an SEO on Upwork: the questions that reveal real skill
item.description: How to vet an SEO consultant on Upwork: the screening questions that expose real skill, what good answers sound like, the red flags, and a safer first step.

item.title: How to change a business name without losing your Google reviews
item.description: How to rename a business without losing its Google Business Profile, reviews, or rankings: edit the existing listing, sequence the change, and update the web.

item.title: Holiday hours on Google: set them before you need them
item.description: How and when to set special hours on Google for Thanksgiving, December, and New Year, when to mark a business temporarily closed, and what searchers see.

item.title: Glossary of SEO and AI search terms
item.description: Plain English definitions of SEO and AI search terms: AEO, GEO, canonical tags, crawl budget, entities, INP, IndexNow, llms.txt, soft 404s, and many more.
